avertissement: Traductions automatiques des textes français ; chaque nombre a été vérifié contre le français. Les documents de la Ville sont en français et font foi.

canopee.description: Tree planting, greening, fighting emerald ash borer and heat islands.
canopee.enBref: This year, the City is paying companies to plant and maintain trees on streets and in parks, and it is funding an organization that plants on private and institutional properties. Boroughs are adding their own money, machinery and teams of employees to plant trees. Two boroughs have also allowed construction projects to deviate from the rules on trees and greening.

etapes.titre: Contracts to plant trees on streets
etapes.texte: City council awards two contracts to 7574479 Canada inc. and Terrassement Technique Sylvain Labrecque inc. to supply and plant 1,374 trees on public land, then water, maintain and replace some of them. The authorized expense is $2,456,590.55, taxes included, and the trees go to seven boroughs, including Saint-Laurent (423), Verdun (281) and Pierrefonds-Roxboro (265).

etapes.titre: Money to plant on private properties
etapes.texte: The City pays $3,071,550 to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain to plant and maintain trees on private and institutional sites from March 24 to December 31, 2026. The organization and its partners in the Alliance forêt urbaine must plant 14,500 trees and 2,500 shrubs in 2026.

Pierrefonds-Roxboro transfers up to $162,233.12 from its parks fund to buy trees and plants. Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve rents a mini-backhoe with operator for $152,916.75 and sets aside $200,000 for additional blue-collar worker teams, with a target of about 1,000 trees planted in 2026.

Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve allows a company to expand its building at 1620, rue Préfontaine with 25 trees and 5% greening, instead of the required 40 trees and 25%, with the company compensating on its other properties. Montréal-Nord allows trees to be planted less than 1.5 metres from the street line at 5745, boulevard Léger, for a two-storey building.

etapes.titre: Work at parc Pratt, in Outremont
etapes.texte: Outremont awards URBEX CONSTRUCTION INC. the renovation of the parc Pratt chalet and the redevelopment of its surroundings, including planting vegetation, water retention and new paths. The authorized expense is $800,416.17, taxes included, funded mainly by the Programme de réfection et de verdissement des parcs locaux.

aSurveiller.texte: The Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain must submit progress reports on July 31 and October 31, 2026, its accountability report by December 31, 2026, at the latest, then its report and financial statements on March 31, 2027.
Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve's tree plantings take place from April or May to November 2026.
Watering, maintenance and replacement of trees planted under the central city's contract continue until the end of November 2029.

deneigement.description: Snow removal and snow loading contracts, spreading of abrasives, parking by-laws.

etapes.texte: Boroughs are renting vacuum sweepers, tanker trucks, sidewalk washers and a mini sweeper with operators to clean streets, alleys, sidewalks and bike paths in the spring. Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve authorizes an expenditure of $574,920.99, taxes included, for four vacuum sweepers and three tanker trucks [CA26 27 0008].

etapes.titre: Snow removal at downtown public squares
etapes.texte: Ville-Marie is hiring companies to maintain, clean and remove snow from square Viger, place des Montréalaises and six squares including square Dorchester and square Victoria. The borough is also extending snow removal at the Quartier des Spectacles by one year, from April 2, 2026 to April 1, 2027 [CA26 24 0067].

etapes.titre: Staff at Verdun's snow disposal site
etapes.texte: Verdun is offering city council to itself provide the staff for the snow disposal site during loading operations, for 2025, 2026 and 2027. The positions concerned are gatehouse attendants, sewer chute monitors, and drivers and operators.

Montréal-Nord approves an additional expenditure of $106,150.97, taxes included, for renting a grader with operator [CA26 10 086]. Saint-Léonard is drawing $200,000 from its surpluses to pay for staff and abrasives [CA26 13 0121].

aSurveiller.texte: Saint-Léonard indicates that the adoption of its snow removal by-law is planned for September 8, 2026, with a notice of coming into force on September 9, 2026.
Extended towing contracts begin on November 15, 2026.
Equipment rental with operator in Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie resumes on November 1, 2026 and runs until March 31, 2027.
The extension of the grader rental contract in Anjou covers November 15, 2026 to April 15, 2027.

eau-egouts.description: Pipes, drinking water production plants, Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant, retention basins.
eau-egouts.enBref: This year, the City is borrowing to finance the disinfection plant at the Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant and new water mains in the Namur–De la Savane sector. It is awarding contracts to rehabilitate water pipes using trenchless methods, rebuild streets along with their sewers and waterworks, and replace lead water service connections. It is also adding funds to projects already underway and purchasing the products and services needed to operate its plants.

etapes.texte: City council is awarding contracts to rehabilitate secondary water pipes through lining, a trenchless technique, and to redo roadways and sidewalks on streets in several boroughs. These contracts also include the replacement of lead water service connections, on both the public and private sides.

The City is adding money to contracts already awarded: $200,000 in contingencies for boulevard De Maisonneuve (CA26 240015) and $1,055,231.53 for the 750 mm pipe on rue Saint-Antoine Ouest (CG26 0153). It is also adding $12,144,522.14 in contingencies for the pipe on rue de la Cathédrale, after an inspection revealed more damaged sections than in 2019 (CG26 0336).

Contracts are being awarded to rebuild water pipes, sewers and roadways together, notably along rue Guy between Saint-Jacques and René-Lévesque, for a total expenditure of $28,921,033.25 (CG26 0245), and on rue De Champlain, where a 1,200 mm main installed in 1927 is being replaced (CG26 0332). Other similar projects affect Saint-Laurent, Lachine, Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles and Pierrefonds-Roxboro.

etapes.titre: Plants, wastewater treatment plant and new loan
etapes.texte: The City is renewing support for the system that controls processes at the Jean-R.-Marcotte plant, extending the purchase of polymers for this plant, adding aluminum sulphate for the Pointe-Claire drinking water production plant, and extending leak detection by probe in water mains. It is also adopting a $12,000,000 loan to build water mains between boulevard Cavendish and rue Isabella, in the Namur–De la Savane sector.

aSurveiller.texte: The pipe along autoroute 15 Nord and the Atwater ramp must be rehabilitated by December 18, 2026 at the latest.
Work on rue de la Cathédrale, up to the McTavish reservoir, must be completed in March 2027.
The rue Guy project must continue until December 2027.
Leak detection in water mains must be completed in June 2028.
The commissioning of the ozone plant at the Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant is expected in 2029.

frederic-back.titre: Parc Frédéric-Back and Complexe environnemental Saint-Michel
frederic-back.description: The former quarry turned dump, being transformed into a park in phases: urban greenhouses, biogas capture, electrical upgrades.
frederic-back.enBref: This year, the City is moving forward on three fronts at parc Frédéric-Back and the Complexe environnemental Saint-Michel: a greenhouse complex in the Saint-Michel neighbourhood, the modernization of electrical facilities linked to biogas capture, and park maintenance. It is also requesting financial assistance from Québec for an east-west pedestrian and cycling link with a footbridge. At the same time, the borough is redeveloping rue De Louvain, along the edge of the park.

etapes.titre: Request for funding for the east-west link
etapes.texte: The City is asking the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable du Québec for assistance of up to $2,000,000 for a 900-metre trail crossing the park from east to west, including a footbridge about 150 metres long (CG26 0121). The project also includes stormwater management works and a 12.7-hectare meadow.

etapes.titre: Greenhouses handed over to the borough
etapes.texte: The urban agglomeration approves the construction of a research, training and community production greenhouse complex, valued at $2,185,000, then delegates the project to city council (CG26 0124). The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension offers to carry it out and city council agrees (CA26 14 0039, CM26 0363).

The City awards Systèmes Urbains inc. a contract for $1,091,693.37, taxes included, for the second phase of electrical work at the Complexe environnemental de Saint-Michel, which includes a new 25 kV power supply, a backup generator and a controller to manage biogas capture (CG26 0223). It is also entrusting two companies with the general maintenance and ecological and horticultural management of the park for 30 months (CG26 0224).

The borough awards Groupe MPotvin the redevelopment of rue De Louvain, between parc Frédéric-Back and boulevard Saint-Michel, for a maximum amount of $8,199,514.82, taxes included, and authorizes total spending of $11,192,464.62. The work covers sewers and water mains, lighting, traffic lights, sidewalks, the bike path and plantings.

The City is extending by five months the rental of a compost screener and a loader tractor with operator at the Complexe environnemental de Saint-Michel, for an additional $296,349.21, taxes included. The compost, made from leaves collected in parks and streets, is used in particular for the development of parc Frédéric-Back (CG26 0320).

The borough awards Les industries Harnois inc. the supply and installation of the greenhouse complex, for a maximum amount of $499,865.92, taxes included, and authorizes total spending of $574,845.80. The project covers two greenhouses with structure, envelope, natural ventilation, ground surfaces, interior divisions and condensation water management.

aSurveiller.texte: Greenhouses: delivery of infrastructure in July 2026, work starting in August 2026 and expected completion in December 2026, according to the borough's file.
Greenhouses expected to come into service in winter 2027.
The call for projects under the ministère des Transports funding program, for the footbridge and the east-west link, ends on November 26, 2026.
Rue De Louvain: work in three phases, from May to November 2026, from May to October 2027, then from May to August 2028.
Park maintenance: contracts from May 1, 2026 to October 31, 2028; 26 hectares will be added to the park in 2027 in the Boisé Ouest sector.
Rental of the screener and loader tractor from June 20 to October 15, 2026.

grand-parc-ouest.description: Canada's largest municipal park, being assembled: land acquisitions, Anse-à-l'Orme, Cap-Saint-Jacques, Bois-de-la-Roche, parc-nature des Sources.

etapes.titre: More money for the stone walls
etapes.texte: The City is adding $162,897.98 to the contract with Les Constructions H2D inc. to redo heritage walls along chemin de Senneville, bringing the contract to $1,174,331.77. According to the file, buried stones, surplus mortar and a deteriorated culvert explain the increase; the work, 60% complete as of December 1, 2025, resumes on May 15, 2026.

etapes.titre: Application for the Cap-Saint-Jacques night sky
etapes.texte: The City is submitting the application for the Cap-Saint-Jacques sector, described as covering 330 hectares, for the international Urban Night Sky Place designation from DarkSky International. The submission involves no spending; the City commits to producing a lighting management plan, upgrading its light fixtures to standards, and keeping the site accessible in the evening.

etapes.titre: Two sectors listed as natural environments
etapes.texte: The City is listing the parc-nature des Sources (38.32 ha) and the Anse-à-l'Orme sector of the Grand parc de l'Ouest (429 ha) in the Répertoire des milieux naturels protégés et contributifs à la biodiversité de l'agglomération, along with conservation plans. It is also taking note of the 2025 summary of areas.

The City is awarding Gendron Gestion Civil inc. the contract to rebuild the culvert under chemin Senneville, as part of the modernization of the pôle agricole du Bois-de-la-Roche, for a total expenditure of $481,850.45. The work includes the new culvert, road resurfacing, and replacement of the guardrails.

aSurveiller.texte: Expected completion of the stone wall work on chemin de Senneville: July 10, 2026.
Submission of the Cap-Saint-Jacques lighting management plan: February 2027.
DarkSky International's response on the designation: April 2027.

itinerance.description: Support for organizations, warming centres and shelters for people experiencing homelessness.
itinerance.enBref: This year, the City is lending municipal buildings free of charge to organizations to open warming centres, and is funding organizations that work with people experiencing homelessness. It is also renewing a Ville-Marie public works team that carries out cleanliness interventions related to homelessness in other boroughs. In June, it set up a framework to accept private donations for housing and shelter projects.

etapes.texte: The City is lending three buildings free of charge for the winter of 2025-2026: the former church at 5600, 12e Avenue in Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie, to the Centre des Femmes de convictions de Montréal; the former Recluses Missionnaires monastery at 12050, boulevard Gouin Est, to Projets Autochtones du Québec; and the former Bain St-Denis at 7075, rue Saint-Hubert, to L'Amour en Action SYL DAN. All three loans end on April 30, 2026.

Verdun is paying $12,950 to the Société de développement social to keep two outreach workers in place from January 5 to February 6, 2026, in municipal facilities and their surroundings. Ahuntsic-Cartierville confirms the continuation of COHAB inc.'s contract to operate a warming centre during the 2025-2026 winter.

etapes.titre: Funding for organizations over three years
etapes.texte: The City grants $5,407,736 to 15 organizations and adds $3,942,461 to 10 already funded organizations, under the Programme itinérance et milieux inclusifs 2026-2028. The projects focus on the inclusion of people experiencing homelessness, cohabitation in public spaces, and awareness-raising.

etapes.titre: Public works team offered to boroughs
etapes.texte: Ville-Marie is offering other boroughs the services of a public works team dedicated to cleanliness related to homelessness, for 12 months starting in spring 2026, with a budget of $931,328 for 2026 coming from the Service de la diversité et de l'inclusion sociale. Le Plateau-Mont-Royal, Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie, Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension, Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve and Le Sud-Ouest accept the offer.

Lachine, Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles and Ahuntsic-Cartierville in turn accept the Ville-Marie team; Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles's agreement runs from May 15, 2026, to May 15, 2027. City council adopts a declaration in support of people experiencing homelessness and in recognition of the organization Maison Mobile.

The City adopts a mechanism to govern private cash donations intended for housing, shelter and social cohabitation projects for people experiencing or at risk of homelessness. Donors do not choose which project is funded, and the City may refuse a donation.

aSurveiller.texte: The agreement on the public works team with Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles runs until May 15, 2027.
Financial support under the Programme itinérance et milieux inclusifs covers a three-year period ending on December 31, 2028.

louvain-est.description: The neighbourhood being built on municipal land in Ahuntsic-Cartierville: acquisitions, soil decontamination, street names, temporary developments.

etapes.texte: City council approved the amendment of two leases for land south of rue de Louvain and west of boulevard Saint-Laurent. One serves as parking for Société de transport de Montréal employee vehicles, the other as paid parking for members of the clicknpark app.

The City is extending the free loan of a 10,000-square-foot lot to Ville en vert for its vegetable garden, a property subsidy valued at $121,100 (CM26 0447). City council also agreed to prepare the lease itself with Îlot 84 for a 78,244-square-foot lot at the southeast corner of rue de Louvain Ouest and avenue de l'Esplanade, free of charge.

The Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension borough awarded Groupe MPotvin the redevelopment of rue de Louvain, between parc Frédéric-Back and boulevard Saint-Michel, for a maximum amount of $8,199,514.82 taxes included. The work covers sewers, water mains, lighting, traffic lights, sidewalks, the bike path and plantings.

etapes.titre: The central street gets a name
etapes.texte: City council named the new street at the heart of the Louvain eco-district "avenue des Solidarités." The name comes from a public call for proposals held in fall 2024 by the borough and the local heritage and toponymy committee.

etapes.titre: New street, networks and decontaminated soil
etapes.texte: The contract goes to Charex inc. to build an eco-district road with sewer, water main, roadway, lighting and environmental soil management, for a total expenditure of $15,366,336 taxes included. The City is adding $2,007,312.15 net, through the environmental liability reserve, to remediate the soil of the former gas station on the Louvain Est site. A one-year free lease is also granted to the Laboratoire sur l'agriculture urbaine for sunflowers and a greenhouse.

aSurveiller.texte: The Esplanade - Louvain temporary space, at 150, rue de Louvain Ouest, is supported for the period from June 9 to December 31, 2026.
The Société de transport de Montréal parking lease starts on October 1, 2026, for three years, for a maximum of 92 days per year.
The land loan to the Laboratoire sur l'agriculture urbaine runs from November 1, 2026 to October 31, 2027.
Ville en vert's vegetable garden can remain in place until December 31, 2027.
The rue de Louvain construction between parc Frédéric-Back and boulevard Saint-Michel takes place in three phases, from May 2026 to August 2028.
Four other public spaces on the site remain to be named before the developments are completed, expected around 2032.

matieres-residuelles.description: Collections, sorting centres, biomethanization and ecocentres.
matieres-residuelles.enBref: The City changed collection schedules and frequencies in several boroughs, and extended contracts for food waste treatment, container collection, and container transport for the Saint-Laurent ecocentre. It also purchased collection bins, awarded companies hydro-excavation work with residual materials treatment, and received the 2025 residual materials management reports.

etapes.titre: Extensions of collection and treatment contracts
etapes.texte: The City extended two contracts with Recyclage Notre-Dame inc. by six months to treat food waste, with an additional expenditure of $3,269,055.43 including taxes [CG26 0045]. It also extended by 12 months the contracts for garbage collection in front-loading and semi-underground containers, and the contract for supplying and transporting containers for the Saint-Laurent ecocentre.

The executive committee changed the collection days, schedules and sectors in L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève, Le Plateau-Mont-Royal and Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve. In Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, garbage is collected every two weeks from November 1 to April 30 and every week from May 1 to October 31 [CE26 0466].

The City entered into agreements with USD Global inc., Orbis Canada ltée and Plasti-Bac inc. to supply and distribute collection bins for residents. Ahuntsic-Cartierville retained Ville en vert to inform and raise awareness among residents of buildings with eight units or fewer in the Ahuntsic and Sault-au-Récollet districts, where the garbage collection frequency is changing, for $230,108.67 including taxes [CA26 09 0141].

Le Plateau-Mont-Royal authorized the removal of two dwelling units in the basement of 397, boulevard Saint-Joseph Ouest to set up a residual materials storage room of at least 28 m² and 32 bicycle spots. Le Sud-Ouest lifted the requirement to set up a drop-off area on the site of the future building at 2380, rue Notre-Dame Ouest, and the executive committee approved an agreement with Tricentris, which is paying $43,773.61 for a program to loan reusable dishware, water fountains and sorting stations.

The urban agglomeration council took note of the 2025 residual materials management report and the accountability report of the 2020-2025 Master Plan: 415 kg of waste per person, 48% of materials diverted from disposal, and 29 of 49 actions completed [CG26 0311]. Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles, Saint-Laurent and Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce filed their expenditure reports for the activities delegated to them.

aSurveiller.texte: The extension of the food waste treatment contracts runs until September 30, 2026.
The container collection contracts and the Saint-Laurent ecocentre container contract are maintained until October 31, 2027.
The program to loan reusable dishware, water fountains and sorting stations is offered until December 31, 2026 at the latest.
The hydro-excavation contracts end on December 31, 2028.

namur-hippodrome.description: The new district on the site of the former Blue Bonnets hippodrome: sale of land, loan by-laws, water supply for the Namur–De la Savane area.

etapes.titre: More time to sell a plot of land
etapes.texte: The Québec government grants the City a deadline of October 31, 2027 to sell a first plot of land on the site, west of boulevard Décarie and south of rue Paré. The extension does not entail any financial compensation and the other conditions of the 2017 transfer remain the same.

The City guarantees a $2,000,000 loan from the Canada Infrastructure Bank to Société GALOPH, a non-profit organization, to pay for feasibility studies for the residential project. The same day, city council rejects a motion from the Official Opposition on governance and management of public assets in the district.

City council adopts a $29,000,000 loan by-law for soil remediation, sewers and water supply, street redevelopment, professional fees and land purchases. This work is meant to serve the first lots of phase 1, intended for social, community and affordable housing.

A second loan by-law, of $12,000,000, funds the construction of water supply main pipes between boulevard Cavendish, in Saint-Laurent, and rue Isabella, in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce. It covers plans and specifications, soil studies, surveying, decontamination, land purchases and a first batch of work.

aSurveiller.texte: October 31, 2027: deadline granted by the Québec government to sell a first plot of land on the site.
2031: the federal grant of $128.3M is conditional on the infrastructure being completed by this date.

parcs.description: Development and renovation of parks, including the Grand parc de l'Ouest.
parcs.enBref: The City is having parks redone in various parts of its territory: play areas, water play areas, trails, sports fields and dog parks. It is awarding design and construction contracts, adjusting contracts already underway, and paying for the decontamination of land where parks will be developed. In the Grand parc de l'Ouest, it is repairing structures, submitting an application for an international designation, and adding a sector to the registry of protected natural environments.

etapes.texte: The City is awarding the winning team of an architecture competition the design of the bibliothèque Caroline-Dawson and the redevelopment of parc Le Prévost, in Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension, for a total expenditure of $10,559,257.81, taxes included. It is also paying $174,471.56 to Verdun for soil studies before redoing the play areas of parc Monseigneur-J.-A.-Richard, developed on a former dump.

etapes.titre: Work and protection in the Grand parc de l'Ouest
etapes.texte: The City is adding $162,897.98 to the contract for the repair of the heritage walls on chemin de Senneville and is awarding a contract to rebuild a culvert under that same road, in the pôle agricole du Bois-de-la-Roche. It is submitting the application for the Cap-Saint-Jacques sector for the Urban Night Sky Place designation and adding the Anse-à-l'Orme sector to the registry of protected natural environments.

etapes.titre: Contracts for redevelopment of neighbourhood parks
etapes.texte: The boroughs are awarding contracts to redo parks: parc à chien Lucie-Bruneau in Anjou, parc Mackenzie-King in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, parc canin Alexis-Nihon in Saint-Laurent, parc Monseigneur-Langlois in Verdun, and parc Percy-Walters in Ville-Marie. Outremont is paying $150,000 to redo the play structure of the parc-école Saint-Germain.

City council is transferring a section of the former rue Eadie, of 810.2 m², to parc Campbell Ouest, in the Sud-Ouest. Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is awarding a construction contract for parc Denise-Morelle and paying a supplement to the project's architects, while LaSalle is awarding the redevelopment of parc J.O.R.-Leduc.

aSurveiller.texte: Parc des Eaux-Cachées public art competition: winner chosen in October 2026, contract in December 2026, artwork installation in 2028.
Urban Night Sky Place application: lighting plan submitted in February 2027, response from DarkSky expected in April 2027, site compliance work in April 2032.
Parc du Bassin-à-Bois: final acceptance of work expected in June 2027.
Parc Denise-Morelle: work from early August 2026 to November 2026.
Parc J.O.R.-Leduc: work from August 2026 to June 2028.
Parc Percy-Walters: work from July to November 2026, with a continuation in spring 2027.

pietonnisation.description: Pedestrian streets, public squares and business animation ordinances.
pietonnisation.enBref: This year, the City and the boroughs are organizing the pedestrian streets for summer 2026: funding to boroughs and business development corporations, then ordinances that close streets to cars and regulate terraces, sales, music and signage. Temporary public squares are also being set up, and support services are being added, such as on-demand transportation on avenue du Mont-Royal.

etapes.titre: Subsidy framework and end of a lawsuit
etapes.texte: Ville-Marie adopts a by-law that allows it to subsidize its business development corporations to pedestrianize streets in 2026, up to $425 per linear metre. Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie settles out of court for $41,686.46 a lawsuit related to work on the public square at the corner of rues Beaubien Est and Boyer.

The executive committee pays $2,694,500 to six boroughs for pedestrian streets on commercial arteries. Ville-Marie and Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce adopt their first ordinances, including the Placette CDN, open from April 1 to October 31, 2026.

Ville-Marie grants $375,500 to the Société de développement commercial du Village for rue Sainte-Catherine Est, and Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension $102,045 for rue Villeray. Outremont sets aside $105,000 for avenue Bernard, in addition to a $106,000 grant from the Service du développement économique.

Outremont closes avenue Bernard from May 19 to September 24, 2026. Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce turns avenues Royal and Madison into pedestrian streets and public squares from June 1 to October 31, 2026. Ville-Marie adjusts the dates of three pedestrianizations.

Le Plateau-Mont-Royal bans amplified instruments and games between 9 p.m. and 8 a.m. on pedestrianized avenues. The City pays $40,000 to animate the pedestrian street Notre-Dame Ouest from July 10 to 19, 2026, and Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce authorizes a business promotion on avenue de Monkland.

aSurveiller.texte: Animation of the pedestrian street Notre-Dame Ouest from July 10 to 19, 2026; the organization must submit its accountability report by August 31, 2026 at the latest.
Avenue de Monkland closed to traffic from August 19 at 10 p.m. to August 24 at 7 a.m., with activities from August 20 to 23, 2026.
Avenue Lacombe closed to cars from September 10 to 13, 2026.
Rue Ontario Est pedestrianized until September 18, 2026; parking meters return on September 17, 2026.
Avenue Bernard fully reopened to traffic as of September 25, 2026.
Placette CDN and avenues Royal and Madison: traffic returns after October 31, 2026, that is November 1, 2026 for the placette.

plan-urbanisme.description: The PUM and the concordance by-laws each borough adopts to comply with it.

etapes.texte: Ahuntsic-Cartierville amended its urban planning by-law for the planting, maintenance, protection and felling of trees. Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie revised three by-laws, and Saint-Léonard two, after public consultations held on February 26 and February 11, 2026.

The borough changed heights, uses and the lot coverage ratio in the sector bounded by avenues Papineau, Émile-Journault and André-Grasset and rue Legendre Est. It also increased the permitted heights on sections of rue Lajeunesse, between boulevards Crémazie and Henri-Bourassa, to follow the Plan's density rules.

Following the public consultation on March 25, 2026, the borough adopted a by-law covering urban planning, special projects, demolition, authorization certificates and cadastral operations. The text authorizes a maximum height of 103 m on the city block of the former terrasse Peel and allows public transit stations in category E.1 sectors.

etapes.titre: Requests for extensions to the ministère
etapes.texte: Ahuntsic-Cartierville requested twelve more months, until June 16, 2027, to adopt its concordance by-laws. L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève requested six more months, citing staff shortages, the complexity of its territory and the fall 2025 election.

aSurveiller.texte: Mid-June 2026: L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève plans to present its project to elected officials, then hold a public consultation in September or October 2026.
June 16, 2027: deadline set by the ministère for Saint-Léonard to adopt all its concordance by-laws; Ahuntsic-Cartierville requested the same deadline.
June 17, 2027: deadline given to Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension to update its by-laws; its zoning by-law must be replaced in 2027.

securite-publique.description: The Service de police de la Ville de Montréal: contracts, neighbourhood police stations, city council motions.

etapes.titre: Loan for equipment and loan of a police officer
etapes.texte: The urban agglomeration council adopts a loan by-law of $10,880,000 to purchase and replace specialized SPVM equipment between 2026 and 2030. It also authorizes the loan of a detective sergeant to the RCMP team that enforces the Firearms Act, starting January 7, 2026.

etapes.titre: Motorcycles, housekeeping, work at the cavalry building
etapes.texte: The City purchases patrol motorcycles, extends the housekeeping service at headquarters by 12 months, and awards a contract to replace the oil heating system of the cavalry building, at 1515, chemin Remembrance. It authorizes a second loan of a police officer to the RCMP, starting March 30, 2026, with a budget of $136,260 for 2026.

etapes.titre: Meals for detainees, software, information campaign
etapes.texte: The City awards a company the preparation and delivery of meals for persons detained by the SPVM, from May 1, 2026 to April 30, 2029. It extends by one year the maintenance of the call dispatch system software and receives a federal grant of $8,000 for a campaign on sexual assaults.

The City enters into an agreement for 9 mm practice ammunition intended for firearms training and extends the SPVM's mail service by one year. It also retains companies for carpentry and painting work in SPVM buildings, and loans a police officer to the Sûreté du Québec team working on the export of stolen vehicles.

aSurveiller.texte: The work to replace the oil heating system at the cavalry building must begin on April 28, 2026 and end on September 30, 2027.
The extension of the call dispatch software maintenance runs until May 4, 2027; the City states it wants to replace this system with a new solution by the end of 2027.
The "Fèves au lard" fundraising activity of neighbourhood police station 46 will be held on October 23, 2026.

transport-collectif.description: What the City decides around the network: land sold to the STM, areas around stations, agreements.
transport-collectif.enBref: This year, the City approved the budget and capital works program of the Société de transport de Montréal (STM), then a loan by-law for the corporation. It also sold or leased land to the STM to expand métro facilities, entrusted the STM with work related to the extension of the blue line and regulated worksites in the métro tunnel. It also signed a letter of no objection for the reconstruction of a bridge-tunnel above the REM.

etapes.texte: The urban agglomeration council adopted the STM's 2026 budget, balanced at $1,804,314,410 in revenues and expenditures, and the 2026-2035 capital works program. The city council gave the same direction.

The City entered into a 36-month agreement with Produits Suncor Énergie for clear diesel and diesel containing renewable fuel, following an STM call for tenders. It also purchased, without a call for tenders, advertising spaces from Astral Affichage in the métro and buses for Espace pour la vie, up to $172,462.50 including taxes.

The City is leasing to the STM a 2,787 square metre lot in Ahuntsic-Cartierville, south of rue de Louvain, as parking for vehicles of officers holding a permit, for a total rent of $49,293. The same borough modified bus waiting posts on its territory as part of the network overhaul.

The City signed an agreement with the STM to build a pavilion in parc Irma-LeVasseur, adjoining the métro ventilation station on avenue Wiseman, in Outremont. It also entrusted the STM with carrying out its municipal work at the future Pie-IX and Viau stations, on rue Jean-Talon Est, for an expenditure of $3,808,451.29 including taxes.

Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce signed a new access agreement with the STM for a vacant lot of 3,274.2 square metres at 4636-4670, boulevard Décarie, and terminated the 2024 transitional occupancy agreement. Ville-Marie authorized the STM to drill and restore the vault of the green line tunnel, between Berri-UQAM and Saint-Laurent, 24 hours a day.

aSurveiller.texte: Drilling and restoration work on the vault of the green line tunnel until July 31, 2026.
Awarding of contracts for the Pie-IX and Viau stations in August and October 2026; opening of the blue line extension stations planned for 2031.
Start of the STM parking lease on October 1, 2026, for three years, at a rate of 92 days per year.
Work on the Rielle ventilation station, in Verdun, until December 2027.
Complete closure of rue Wilderton, for a maximum of two weeks, during the 2027 summer holidays; bridge-tunnel reconstruction work from June 2026 to March 2028.

velo.titre: Cycling: REV, bike paths and BIXI
velo.description: The Réseau express vélo, bike paths and lanes, and the BIXI bike-sharing system.
velo.enBref: This year, the City is buying bikes, docks and station parts for the BIXI system, and having new stations installed at street work sites. It is also funding the repair of existing bike paths, including the REV Lajeunesse, and regularizing rents for Hydro-Québec land crossed by bike paths. Boroughs, for their part, oversee the development and maintenance of their own bike paths.

etapes.texte: Outremont authorizes a $100,000 expenditure, taxes included, for concrete, de-icing salt and abrasives intended in particular for bike paths. Ahuntsic-Cartierville awards Déneigement et Excavation M. Gauthier inc. the rental, with operator, of a mini sweeper for spring cleaning of paths less than 1.8 metres wide, for $153,395.05, taxes included.

etapes.titre: Sustainable mobility corridors in the east end
etapes.texte: City council adds $3,400,000, taxes included, to the contract with Bruneau Électrique inc. for traffic lights, civil and electrical work, and bike paths in Ville-Marie and Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, on rue Hochelaga and rue du Havre. The contract reaches $11,399,999.99, taxes included.

City council approves a $125,167.62 agreement, taxes included, with Hydro-Québec for rents from 2014 to 2025 on 19 plots of land used for bike paths, parks and community gardens. It then approves a 10-year lease, at a total rent of $46,896, taxes included, to rent about 366 square metres in Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles for bike path purposes.

etapes.titre: Repair of the REV Lajeunesse and rue Lajoie
etapes.texte: Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension offers to take charge of repairing sections of the REV Lajeunesse, between rue Jarry and boulevard Crémazie, and city council accepts this offer as well as one from Ville-Marie for roadway and bike path work under the 2019 Bike Plan. Outremont tables a draft by-law to convert the shared lane on avenue Lajoie, between Stuart and Outremont, into a one-way bike path.

aSurveiller.texte: For the REV Lajeunesse, the file indicates a call for tenders in May 2026, contract awards in June, and work from July to August 2026.
The UCI Road World Championships are held in Montréal from September 20 to 27, 2026; sections along the route are targeted by roadway work in Ville-Marie.
The repair of the bike path on rue De Louvain, between west of rue d'Iberville and boulevard Saint-Michel, is listed at $570,000 in 2027.
Work on the sustainable mobility corridors resumes in spring 2026, for delivery in spring or summer 2026.
